extracted.intended_audience: economists, researchers, NBER affiliates, and prospective affiliates
extracted.subtask_description: An organizational overview of the National Bureau of Economic Research's programs and working groups, describing each program's topical scope and the organizational/meeting requirements for programs and working groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programs correspond to traditional fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Research programs are the backbone of the NBER. Each of the 19 programs corresponds loosely to a traditional field of study within economics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each NBER affiliate is associated with one or more programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs are led by a Director or co-Directors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program meeting frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs host at least two meetings each year, including one at the NBER Summer Institute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economics of Aging (program scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Program on the Economics of Aging studies the health and economic circumstances of individuals as they age with particular emphasis on late-life experiences, as well as the broader economic consequences of population aging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset Pricing (program scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Asset Pricing Program explores the factors that determine the prices of and returns on financial and real assets, including stocks, bonds, currencies, and real estate. It also studies the behavior of households and firms that invest in these assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children and Families (program scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Program on Children and Families uses economic tools to study the factors that inform the wellbeing of children and families. It considers the role of education, public and private health insurance, and transfer programs, as well as the long-run economic and social consequences of early-life circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate Finance (program scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Corporate Finance Program explores the determinants and consequences of the financing decisions made by firms and households. It also encompasses corporate governance, household finance, and the links between the real and financial sectors of the economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development Economics (program scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Development Economics Program studies the forces that contribute to economic development, particularly in less developed nations. It explores the role of decisions by households, firms, and governments, the effects of development aid policies, and the consequences of rising incomes in emerging economies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of the American Economy (program scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Program on the Development of the American Economy explores the sources of long-run growth and fluctuations in the US economy. It considers the contributions of human and physical capital, as well as the role of public policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic Fluctuations and Growth (program scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Economic Fluctuations and Growth Program investigates both long-term trends and short-term fluctuations in aggregate employment, output, and prices. It explores the nature of business cycles, particularly in the United States, as well as the effects of monetary and fiscal policy on economic performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economics of Education (program scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Education Program studies the effect of education on individuals’ earnings and other outcomes, as well as the effect of educational inputs and education policies on student achievement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economics of Health (program scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers affiliated with the Economics of Health Program study the economic determinants of health, the operation of health care markets, and the financing of health care with particular emphasis on public and private insurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core topics of interest include the determinants of "health capital" and the consequences of unhealthy behaviors such as substance abuse, the role of market failure in health care and health insurance markets, and the impact of public policies on health care delivery, expenditures, financing, and innovation. The program is the successor to the Health Care and Health Economics Programs, which merged in July 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment and Energy Economics (program scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Environment and Energy Economics Program studies the economics of the energy sector, the determinants of pollution and other actions that affect the environment, and the effects of public policies in both of these areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial Organization (program scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Industrial Organization Program analyzes firm behavior and industry dynamics, including the determinants of market competition and of pricing decisions, as well as the effects of public policies such as anti-trust law and government regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Finance and Macroeconomics (program scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Finance and Macroeconomics Program studies financial interactions among nations, including cross-border capital flows, exchange rates, responses to global financial crises, and transmission of economic shocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Trade and Investment (program scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Trade and Investment Program examines the causes and consequences of trade between and among nations and regions. It considers how transportation costs, tariffs, and other factors affect geographic specialization and commercial flows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor Studies (program scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Labor Studies Program explores issues related to employment and compensation, including the supply of and demand for labor, human capital, and the determinants and consequences of unemployment. It also considers the effects of labor unions and policies such as minimum wages and training programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law and Economics (program scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Law and Economics Program studies the economic causes and consequences of specific legal rules as well as the impact of the broader legal system. It encompasses the behavior of firms and individuals, and considers property rights, deterrence, and the effects of law enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetary Economics (program scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Monetary Economics Program studies the conduct and effects of monetary policy, including its impact on interest rates and inflation, and the consequences of policy actions by central banks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It also considers macroeconomic forces that impinge on central bank decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political Economy (program scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Political Economy Program examines the interactions among political institutions, participants in the political system, such as voters and elected officials, and economic outcomes broadly defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Productivity, Innovation, and Entrepreneurship (program scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Productivity, Innovation, and Entrepreneurship Program studies firm-level and economy-wide forces that determine productivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It emphasizes the factors that affect innovation, patenting, entrepreneurship, and the creation of new firms, while also exploring broader issues such as the productivity effects of firms’ investment spending and the composition of the labor force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Economics (program scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Economics Program explores the efficiency and distributional effects of various tax policies and government spending programs, as well as the way that these programs affect the behavior of households and firms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working groups: relative formality
rubrics_metrics.description: Working groups are less formal than programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working groups: affiliation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Working groups do not have affiliated researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working groups: meeting frequency and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Working group directors convene one or two meetings each year, bringing together both NBER affiliates and other researchers who are working on particular topic areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral Finance (working group scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Behavioral Finance Working Group studies financial markets using approaches grounded in psychological research, with applications in asset pricing, corporate finance, and household finance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chinese Economy (working group scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chinese Economy Working Group studies the Chinese economy, convening meetings in both the U.S. and China.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core topic areas include development and growth, labor and housing markets, macroeconomic, trade, and financial policies, and demographic change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economics of Crime (working group scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Crime Working Group studies economic elements of the causes and consequences of crime, with particular emphasis on interventions in the criminal justice system and elsewhere that may lower crime rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entrepreneurship (working group scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Entrepreneurship Working Group studies the dynamics of firm creation and the factors that influence it, including the career choices of entrepreneurs and the capital market and regulatory environment facing young firms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender in the Economy (working group scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: This working group provides a venue for explicitly anchoring research discussions on gender-related economic topics, bringing together researchers from different fields of economics who are working on these topics to share and discuss current research findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research describes constraints (insufficient access to formal financial services, work, and education, disempowering social norms, and gender‑biased laws and institutions) and evaluates interventions to remove them; activities build on a prior Study Group on Gender and the Economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Household Finance (working group scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Household Finance Working Group studies household saving, portfolio behavior, borrowing, and investment decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It considers the effects of regulation and other public policies, as well as innovations in the market environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation Policy (working group scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Innovation Policy Working Group studies the determinants and consequences of innovation, with particular attention to patent policy, public support for research, and the interactions between firms, universities, and government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insurance (working group scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Insurance Working Group studies the demand for insurance products by households and firms, the role of regulations and other factors in affecting insurance market equilibrium, and the interaction between publicly- and privately-provided insurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market Design (working group scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Market Design Working Group studies market institutions such as auctions, queues, assignment rules in school systems, clearinghouses, and tradeable permit systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It emphasizes the role of institutional design in determining market outcomes and the well-being of market participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Economics (working group scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organizational Economics Working Group studies the structures that govern non-market transactions, such as transactions within firms, government agencies, and non-profit organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It also considers the boundaries of the firm and the role of contracts and other structures that mediate transactions between firms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel Economics (working group scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Personnel Economics Working Group studies human resource questions that arise within firms, including hiring, promotion policy, the design of cash compensation and benefit packages, and outsourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Race and Stratification in the Economy (working group scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Working Group on Race and Stratification in the Economy explores the role of public policies, private practices, and historical factors in contributing to and ameliorating racial disparities in economic outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Urban Economics (working group scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Urban Economics Working Group studies the economics of cities and the many policies and factors that determine city structure and performance, such as land use restrictions, local labor markets, agglomeration economies, trade, and transportation infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: NBER dissemination channels
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to working papers, the NBER disseminates affiliates’ latest findings through a range of free periodicals — the NBER Reporter, the NBER Digest, the Bulletin on Health, and the Bulletin on Entrepreneurship — as well as online conference reports, video lectures, and interviews.
